about: The inside of the spleen, drawn as anatomy: the fibrous capsule, the trabeculae that run in from it, the red pulp, the white pulp follicles with their marginal zone, the splenic artery and vein, and the hilum where they enter and leave. Arterial blood runs in at the hilum and filtered blood leaves by the vein, at a speed that follows the cardiac output; the white pulp brightens when the model reports immune activation, infection or inflammation, and the red pulp when it reports red cells being broken down. The branch paths, the number and size of the follicles (a couple of dozen beads, vastly larger and fewer than the real thing), the capsule thickness and the vessel sizes are drawing choices, not measurements. The splenic sinuses, the lymphatics, the nerves and the tiny red pulp cords are left out, and no cell counts or flow rates are shown.

GH14.label: Hall JE, Hall ME. Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th ed. Elsevier, 2021.

GRAYS42.label: Standring S (ed). Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice, 42nd ed. Elsevier, 2020.

parts.label: Fibrous Capsule
parts.summary: The tough fibrous covering of the spleen
parts.function: The capsule is a thin, tough layer of connective tissue covered by peritoneum. It holds the soft pulp in shape and sends extensions, the trabeculae, into the organ. It is drawn as a faint glass skin, and the spleen's reservoir of blood can be released when the body needs it, as in blood loss.

drives.note: The spleen holds a reservoir of blood that is released when blood is lost.
Sympathetic outflow squeezes blood out of the spleen's reservoir.

parts.label: Trabeculae
parts.summary: Fibrous cords that run in from the capsule and hilum
parts.function: The trabeculae are strands of connective tissue that run inwards from the capsule and the hilum, dividing the organ into compartments and carrying the larger vessels. They are drawn as thin solid cords from the hilum to the capsule so that they can be picked.

drives.note: The supporting framework tightens a little when sympathetic outflow is raised.

parts.label: Red Pulp
parts.summary: The blood-filled meshwork that filters and stores blood
parts.function: Red pulp makes up most of the spleen: cords and sinuses full of blood, lined with macrophages. It removes old and damaged red cells and particles from the blood passing through, and holds a reserve of blood. It is drawn as glass and brightens when red cells are being broken down.

drives.note: Red pulp macrophages remove damaged or broken red cells.
The red pulp also filters microbes and debris from the blood.

parts.label: White Pulp Follicles
parts.summary: Lymphoid follicles around the small central arterioles
parts.function: White pulp is lymphoid tissue, sheaths and follicles of lymphocytes round the branches of the splenic artery. It is where the spleen mounts an immune response to blood-borne microbes. The follicles are drawn as solid beads that brighten and whiten when the model reports immune activation or infection.

drives.note: Lymphoid tissue is activated by an immune response.
Blood-borne pathogens are met by the white pulp.

parts.label: Marginal Zone
parts.summary: The border where blood first meets the white pulp
parts.function: The marginal zone is a rim round each follicle where blood from the arterioles slows and filters through, so that its cells can sample what the blood carries. It is the spleen's first immune contact with blood-borne microbes. It is drawn as a glass shell round each follicle, more visible when the immune response is strong.

drives.note: Blood-borne microbes are sampled here first.
Its cells take part in the early immune response.

parts.label: Splenic Artery
parts.summary: The artery that brings blood in at the hilum
parts.function: The splenic artery arrives at the hilum, divides into branches that follow the trabeculae, and gives off small central arterioles into the white pulp. Its blood is drawn in the arterial colour, running in at a speed that follows the cardiac output, so it slows when the output falls.

drives.note: More blood flows through the organ when cardiac output is higher.
Less blood flows through it when output falls.

parts.label: Splenic Vein
parts.summary: The vein that carries filtered blood out at the hilum
parts.function: Blood that has passed through the red pulp drains into veins that follow the arteries out of the hilum and join to form the splenic vein, which goes on to the portal vein. Its blood is drawn in the venous colour, leaving at the same speed as the inflow.

drives.note: More blood drains from the organ when cardiac output is higher.
Less blood drains from it when output falls.

parts.label: Hilum
parts.summary: The cleft on the inner surface where vessels enter and leave
parts.function: The hilum is the slit on the visceral surface of the spleen where the splenic artery and vein, and the nerves, enter and leave the organ. The tail of the pancreas reaches it. It is drawn as a thin solid cord along the cleft.

drives.note: More blood passes in and out when output is higher.

parts.label: Gastrosplenic Ligament
parts.summary: Fold of peritoneum from the stomach to the hilum (schematic extent)
parts.function: It joins the stomach to the front of the hilum and carries the short gastric vessels. Drawn as a thin sheet; its extent here is a drawing choice.

parts.label: Splenorenal Ligament
parts.summary: Fold of peritoneum from the left kidney to the hilum (schematic extent)
parts.function: It joins the hilum to the region of the left kidney and carries the splenic vessels. Drawn as a thin sheet; its extent here is a drawing choice.

parts.label: Periarteriolar Lymphoid Sheath
parts.summary: Lymphoid tissue wrapped round each central arteriole (schematic)
parts.function: A sleeve of T lymphocytes around the arteriole inside a white-pulp follicle.

parts.label: Germinal Centre
parts.summary: A zone where B cells multiply in a follicle (schematic)
parts.function: Present when a follicle is responding to an antigen, where B cells multiply and improve their antibodies. It comes and goes; the drawing shows a few as a device.

parts.label: Central Arteriole
parts.summary: The small artery running through a white-pulp follicle
parts.function: A branch of the splenic artery that runs through the middle of the lymphoid sheath, bringing blood to the white pulp.

parts.label: Splenic Cords (of Billroth)
parts.summary: The cellular meshwork between the sinuses (schematic)
parts.function: Tissue between the venous sinuses where blood slowly filters past macrophages and old or damaged red cells are held and removed.

parts.label: Venous Sinuses
parts.summary: Wide, leaky vessels that drain the red pulp
parts.function: Blood from the cords passes through the sinus walls and drains toward the splenic vein. Drawn as a few tubes; real sinuses are far more numerous.

parts.label: Red Pulp Macrophages
parts.summary: Cells that engulf old red cells and debris (schematic)
parts.function: They remove worn-out red cells and cell debris from the blood. Drawn as beads far larger than real cells.

parts.label: Trabecular Arteries
parts.summary: Branches of the splenic artery inside the trabeculae
parts.function: After entering at the hilum the artery divides into branches that run in the supporting trabeculae.

parts.label: Penicillar Arterioles
parts.summary: Brush-like fine terminal arterioles opening into the red pulp (schematic)
parts.function: Small arterioles that leave the white pulp and split like the hairs of a brush, delivering blood to the red pulp.
